description: We are a team driven by creativity and a shared love for technology.
summary: GaryshCare is a prototype health-monitoring system for NASA astronauts on long-duration space missions. We do our analysis and health tracking through wearable sensors, modeled on the CSA Bio-Monitor smart shirt, which capture ECG, blood pressure, SpO₂, respiration, and temperature. The app assesses these indicators and shows astronauts a clear status (normal, watch, alert, or critical) by directing them on what to do next. There is also an AI-powered assistant that predicts changes in health indicators over the next 15 and 30 minutes and provides simple, easy-to-understand explanations and recommendations to help astronauts take preventive action. This allows them not to wait until coming back to Earth. Reports from the app are sent automatically to flight surgeons. In addition, a wellbeing module implements breathing exercises and meditation when the system shows stress or poor sleep. All thresholds and recommendations are grounded in NASA sources, while any custom rules we built are labeled as an 'app rule.' Sensor data is simulated.
details: GaryshCare - Garysh means Space, and Garysker means Astronaut in the Kazakh language. This app is created to monitor astronauts' health for deep-space missions. We used Python 3 programming language, FastAPI and WebSockets (sensor simulator, assessment engine, communication channel) for backend. For Frontend React, TypeScript, Vite and Recharts were used. The AI part was built in Python with scikit-learn, pandas and NumPy: an Isolation Forest model detects unusual vital-sign patterns, gradient boosting models forecast vitals 15 to 30 minutes ahead, and the models were trained on data generated by our sensor simulator. Background photo from the NASA Image and Video Library (ISS030-E-055569). NASA-STD-3001 requires missions to monitor vital-sign trends and ECG, transmit medical data privately to Earth, and support autonomous medical care and evidence-based behavioral protocols on electronic devices. NASA's Human Research Program also names arrhythmias and low blood pressure with fainting after gravity changes as cardiovascular risks, and Mars communication delay reaches up to 20 minutes one way. The CSA Bio-Monitor already measures vitals on the ISS. We add onboard assessment, guidance and report triage on top of it.
